messages.author: 8d4d06c10c4d67c9
messages.subject: Using stan with non-rectangular data
parts:
Hi,

My data are vectors of observed values from subgroups within groups: for each subgroup s, from group g I have a vector with n_sg number of observations, where each n_sg maybe different for every s and every g. My question is whether stan handles such non-rectangular data? I've noticed a post from several months back mentioning that it is on the todo list and was wondering whether it is already implemented.

Thanks a lot

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Using stan with non-rectangular data
parts:
Your suggestion sounds like an R's data.frame - with the following indices:
Group Subgroup ObservationIndex ObservedValue
1        1              1                       0.55
1        1              2                       0.64
.
.
1       g1s1          n_g1s1              0.24
.
.
gG    gGsS         n_gGsS             0.76

Where G is the total number of groups and S is the total number of subgroups (S is identical for each group in my data).
As far as I understood from stan's manual, however, it doesn't seem that such a representation is possible. The equivalent to such a data.frame in stan would be something like a 2D array (with dimensions GxS), where each element in that array is a vector of size n_gs and these n_gs's are different for every gs, So the question is whether such an array possible in stan? or is there any other way to represent my data?

Thanks

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Using stan with non-rectangular data
parts:
No, there is nothing that lets you explicitly represent
rectangular data in Stan yet.

As an alternative, look at the coding of the LDA model
in the manual. It provides a representation for
a sequence of documents, each of a different number of
categorical observations.

As you mentioned in the follow-up, it does in fact
look a bit like an R data frame.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Using stan with non-rectangular data
parts:
On Tuesday, February 19, 2013 9:51:05 AM UTC-5, rubi wrote:
My data are vectors of observed values from subgroups within groups: for each subgroup s, from group g I have a vector with n_sg number of observations, where each n_sg maybe different for every s and every g. My question is whether stan handles such non-rectangular data? I've noticed a post from several months back mentioning that it is on the todo list and was wondering whether it is already implemented.

As Bob mentioned, there is no great way to handle data like this in Stan. However, depending on the details of your problem and my remembering of stuff that I haven't actually tried in a while, something like the following might work

data{
  int<lower=1> n_max;   // maximum of n_sg
  int<lower=1> J;       // number of groups
  int<lower=1> K;       // number of covariates
  matrix[n_max,K] X[J]; // array of matrices, one for each group
  // all but one matrix will have too many rows so you have to keep track
  int<lower=1> n_sg[J];
}

Basically, in the other blocks of your stan file, you have to take into consideration that X[j] may have empty rows at the bottom. Depending on the problem, maybe you can fill with zeros at the bottom or maybe you just have to be careful to only loop over n_sg[j] rows or whatever.

Like I said, not ideal but possibly viable.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Using stan with non-rectangular data
parts:
I think

matrix<lower=0,upper=1>[S,K] X[G];

A matrix can only have real numbers, so it is unnecessary to incorporate "real" into the declaration somewhere. The only things that can be ints are scalars and arrays, e.g.

int<lower=1> N;
int<lower=0,upper=1> y[N];

Ben
